benchmarks.system: PSR mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement (in force 7 Oct 2024) via Faster Payments and CHAPS
benchmarks.what_it_does: Sending and receiving PSPs split reimbursement of authorised-push-payment scam losses (cap GBP 85,000, GBP 100 excess). It moves the loss onto banks, which creates the incentive to stop mule accounts; it does not itself prescribe how a receiving bank holds funds.
benchmarks.numbers: 88% of money lost reimbursed over 18 months (7 Oct 2024-31 Mar 2026); GBP 316m reimbursed over 18 months; GBP 72.6m in Q1 2026; about 438,300 claims reported, 301,500 in scope; 82% closed within 5 business days; PSR estimates GBP 73m a year lower APP losses and about 35,000 fewer scams
benchmarks.gap: Victim-side compensation and sender-side friction. Nothing computes a proportionate, per-account hold on the receiving (mule) side from a traced money trail; an innocent recipient's account is not addressed.

benchmarks.system: Protection from Scams Act (in force 1 Jul 2025) restriction orders; Anti-Scam Centre; proposed account disabling orders (Bill announced 4 Aug 2026)
benchmarks.what_it_does: Police can order banks to restrict a likely scam VICTIM's account, ATM and credit use for up to 30 days, with up to 5 extensions; funds stay usable for daily expenses at police discretion. A proposed Bill adds disclosure orders and orders to disable accounts matching scam-related indicators (up to 30 days, extendable once by up to 30 days; appeal to Commissioner of Police). A facility-restriction framework for mules (from Oct 2025) can run up to 3 years.
benchmarks.numbers: H1 2026: 16,821 scam cases, S$410.6m lost, S$97m+ recovered by Anti-Scam Centre, 18 restriction orders issued; 2025: scam cases down 27.6%, more than 7,000 mules and suspects investigated; 2024 record losses S$1.1bn, 50,000+ cases
benchmarks.gap: Orders are person- or indicator-level (restrict the individual or disable the account for up to 30 days). Neither computes an amount-proportionate lien from a traced trail, and a disabled account is not partially held.
benchmarks.source: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c2k1148dwdwo (1 Jul 2025, opened by curl) ; https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/scams-banks-telcos-disclose-info-disable-accounts-ocha-fines-6294631 (4 Aug 2026, opened by curl) ; https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/courts-crime/over-410m-lost-to-scams-in-first-half-of-2026-8-in-10-victims-voluntarily-handed-money-to-scammers (26 Aug 2026, opened by curl)

benchmarks.system: Scam-Safe Accord (banks), Fraud Reporting Exchange (FRX) run by AFCX, National Anti-Scam Centre, Scams Prevention Framework
benchmarks.what_it_does: FRX lets member banks report scam-receiving accounts to each other quickly; Accord commits banks to confirmation of payee, warnings, payment delays and limits on high-risk channels; the Scams Prevention Framework gives banks, telcos and platforms mandatory anti-scam obligations (from 1 Jul 2026 per Australian Broker).
benchmarks.numbers: A$100m industry confirmation-of-payee system; all ABA and COBA members joined AFCX/FRX by Jul 2024 (page gives no member count); A$2.18bn total scam losses in 2025 (investment A$837.7m, up 7.8%); A$248.3m lost in Q1 2026 across 60,657 reports
benchmarks.gap: Information exchange and friction. No hold-duration rule or amount-proportionate hold is specified; the receiving bank decides how much to freeze. FRX volume and funds-frozen figures were not published on the pages opened.

benchmarks.system: FinCEN Section 314(b) voluntary information sharing; Zelle (Early Warning Services) scam claims
benchmarks.what_it_does: 314(b) gives banks a safe harbor to share information with each other on suspected money laundering and (per FinCEN's 12 Jun 2026 fact sheet issue) fraud and other specified unlawful activity. There is no national freeze/lien procedure for scam proceeds; holds are each bank's own policy.
benchmarks.numbers: Fact sheet reissued 12 Jun 2026 (FinCEN page does not give participant counts). Senator Warren report: Zelle-owning banks reimbursed 47% of dollars customers reported as unauthorized in 2021 and H1 2022 (Bank of America about 45%, $56.1m of $125m; PNC 14% of cases); industry reply: 99.9% of 5bn Zelle transactions had no reported fraud or scam
benchmarks.gap: Voluntary, bilateral sharing and no tracing-to-hold computation; recipients' accounts are held (or not) at bank discretion with no proportionality standard.

benchmarks.system: Instant Payments Regulation Verification of Payee (VoP); PSR/PSD3 package (provisional deal 27 Nov 2025)
benchmarks.what_it_does: VoP makes euro-area PSPs confirm payee name and account number before a SEPA credit transfer (mandatory since Oct 2025; non-euro PSPs by Jul 2027). It stops misdirected/impersonation payments before they are made.
benchmarks.numbers: VoP mandatory euro-area from Oct 2025, non-euro area Jul 2027 (LSEG); LSEG cites projected global APP fraud losses of US$331bn by 2027
benchmarks.gap: Pre-payment check only. It does not handle funds that have already landed in a mule account, and there is no tracing or proportionate hold. PSR/PSD3 details not verified in this pass (headline-only).

gtm.fact: A Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre (CFMC) at I4C seats representatives of major banks, financial intermediaries, payment aggregators, telecom providers, IT intermediaries and state/UT law enforcement together for real-time action; this is the existing integration point LienLine would sit beside.

MHA SOP for NCRP-CFCFRMS (complaint processing, bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, restoration) is in force; Money Restoration and Grievance Redressal modules functional from April 2026. LienLine automates the lien-sizing and clock-keeping the SOP presumes.

MuleHunter.AI (RBI Innovation Hub) is deployed across 31 banks for mule detection (detection only, upstream of LienLine); RBIH advertises 85%+ accuracy. Headline: RBIH nudging banks to adopt it (ET BFSI, 19 May 2026, link not opened).

Supreme Court (4 Aug 2026) directed RBI to adopt a debit-hold SOP within 4 weeks and states to operationalise the grievance/restoration modules; RBI issued draft KYC Amendment Directions on 11 Sep 2026 (bank-placed temporary debit hold, 60-day cap, central MIS of holds). This creates a compliance deadline-driven demand window for banks.

MP HC (Archana, 27 Jul 2026) and Rajasthan HC (Shree Balaji Enterprises, 20 Aug 2026) issue statewide freeze guidelines; Rajasthan HC orders a DGP circular in 4 weeks and RBI-run training for bank staff in 8 weeks. Police headquarters and bank nodal officers are the named buyers/users.
